subject: can you use an html ui and also use the list form of runApp()?

messages.author: 4184023bb084c468
messages.subject: can you use an html ui and also use the list form of runApp()?
parts:
I prefer the list form of runApp() because it fits better into packages and seems to me to encourage code reuse.

I was wondering if (and how) an app could use a custom HTML UI and also work with the list form of runApp().

I tried this with example 8 and it didn't work. I basically pasted the contents of server.R (minus the library(shiny) line) and tried this:

runApp(list(server=shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  # Reactive expression to generate the requested distribution. This is 
  # called whenever the inputs change. The output expressions defined 
  # below then all used the value computed from this expression
  data <- reactive({
    dist <- switch(input$dist,
                   norm = rnorm,
                   unif = runif,
                   lnorm = rlnorm,
                   exp = rexp,
                   rnorm)
    
    dist(input$n)
  })
  
  # Generate a plot of the data. Also uses the inputs to build the 
  # plot label. Note that the dependencies on both the inputs and
  # the data reactive expression are both tracked, and all expressions 
  # are called in the sequence implied by the dependency graph
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    dist <- input$dist
    n <- input$n
    
    hist(data(), 
         main=paste('r', dist, '(', n, ')', sep=''))
  })
  
  # Generate a summary of the data
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    summary(data())
  })
  
  # Generate an HTML table view of the data
  output$table <- renderTable({
    data.frame(x=data())
  })
  
})))

It started an app but the contents just said "not found". Is there a way to specify that the UI should come from the 'www' directory?

Thanks.

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: can you use an html ui and also use the list form of runApp()?
parts:
Sorry, when you use runApp() this way, it won't look for a www/ directory. You'll need to create a directory with a server.R file and a www/ subdirectory, then runApp() on the directory.

This won't solve your immediate issue, but in general if you want to reuse code, you can write a function that calls shinyApp(), which will return a shiny.appobj object. The print.shiny.appobj() method calls runApp(), so if the function call returns such an object to the console, it'll automatically run the app.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: can you use an html ui and also use the list form of runApp()?
parts:
Is there any way that capability could be added? 

Currently I"m looking at  a package that contains a shiny app, the shiny app code lives in inst/server.R and the custom ui is in inst/www.

When I run R CMD check on this package I get a NOTE saying:

Namespaces in Imports field not imported from:
  MSGFplus mzR shinyFiles xlsx

This is because there are packages required by server.R but R doesn't know about them because server.R is not in the R directory of the package.

Having the list option to runApp() was a big leap forward in integrating shiny into packages, but this is a bit of a problem....It would be nice if all package infrastructure such as R CMD check could be aware of shiny code. Is it possible to make that happen?

Thanks,
Dan
